why: Definition item: only LocalModel.HasApproxProperty is listed, so A = True and both implications are vacuous. The content is B itself, proved outright as B_holds. The two definitions differ only in how the open V ⊆ O is presented. The project uses an open W ⊆ E₀ with cl_E(O ∩ W) ⊆ O and supports (taken in O) ⊆ W. B uses V = O ∩ W' with cl_C(V) = cl_E(V) ∩ C ⊆ O and supports ⊆ V. With V = O ∩ W these agree: a support taken in O lies in W iff it lies in O ∩ W, and cl_E(V) ∩ C = cl_E(V) because V ⊆ O ⊆ C and the partial quadrant C is closed (LocalModel.O_subset_C, LocalModel.isPartialQuadrant). All other clauses are literally the same: f continuous on O, [0, 1]-valued on O; g IsScSmoothRetractMap into realSc, [0, 1]-valued; |f − g| ≤ ε on O for every ε > 0.
overlap: B_to_A trivial (0). A_to_B (via B_holds) against the definition HasApproxProperty: 8 shared items, all auto-generated sc-scale glue of realSc (ScBanach.constScale proofs, ScScale.mem_smooth_iff). B_holds itself uses only LocalModel.O_subset_C and LocalModel.isPartialQuadrant (Chapter 2).
